entities.title: Invite anyone by email
entities.summary: A player invites a friend by email address, whether or not the friend has played before.
entities.statement: A signed-in player can invite any email address to an online game and choose their colour; the friend finds the invitation when they sign in with that address, gets an email when sending is set up, and the inviter gets a link to send either way.
entities.rationale: GDD pillar 2, Play anyone, any time.
acceptanceCriteria: An invitation to an address nobody has used yet is waiting when someone signs in with it.
Without email set up, the inviter still gets a working link.

origin.description: Pillar 2: invitations go to an email address; a game waits as long as it needs to.

entities.title: Play at your own pace
entities.summary: An online game waits as long as it needs to; either player can leave and come back days later.
entities.statement: Online games have no clocks; a game in play is kept on the server and opens again where it was.
entities.rationale: Correspondence-style chess between friends in different places.
acceptanceCriteria: A game left for days opens at the same position with its whole transcript.
Whose move it is shows in the lobby.

origin.description: Pillar 2 and the decision log: no clocks, correspondence-style games.

entities.title: The server is the referee
entities.summary: Every online move and message is checked on the server.
entities.statement: The server checks every online action (turn, legality, offers) with chess.js before it is saved, and both players get the game as the server has it.
entities.rationale: GDD pillar 4: neither player's client can be trusted with the other's game.
acceptanceCriteria: An illegal move, a move out of turn or a stale one is refused and the board put back.
Only the game's two players can act in it.
Two actions on one game never race.

origin.description: Pillar 4: online moves are checked on the server.

entities.title: A game is a conversation
entities.summary: Moves and chat share one transcript, with times, kept and replayable.
entities.statement: Every move, message, draw offer, refusal, resignation and result goes into the game's transcript with the time it happened; the transcript is kept with the game and shown in play and in replay.
acceptanceCriteria: The transcript lists moves and messages in the order they happened, with clock times and how long each move took.
Chat works during and after the game.

origin.description: Pillar 3: moves and chat share one transcript, with times, kept forever and replayable.

entities.title: Replays at the game's own pace
entities.summary: A finished game plays back at the pace it was played, sped up.
entities.statement: History lists every finished game; a replay steps through it, or plays it at 1×, 4× or 16× the pace it was played, with pauses capped at three seconds.
entities.rationale: Reliving a game, chat and timing included.
acceptanceCriteria: Play, Back, Next, the slider and the moves in the transcript all move the replay.
No pause in playback is longer than three seconds.

origin.description: Decision log: replays play back at the game's own pace, sped up 1×, 4× or 16×, with pauses capped at 3 s.

entities.title: Contacts are the people you have played
entities.summary: Everyone a player has played is a contact, with the record against them.
entities.statement: A contact is made when an invitation is accepted; it shows name, address, picture and wins, losses and draws, opens to every game together, and can be invited again or removed.
entities.rationale: Finding friends again; contacts cannot be added by hand.
acceptanceCriteria: Accepting an invitation makes each the other's contact; an invitation alone does not.
The record counts finished online games from the owner's side.

origin.description: Decision log: contacts are the people you have played, with your history against each.

entities.title: Play the computer at eight strengths
entities.summary: Stockfish in the browser, from beginner to full strength.
entities.statement: A player can play Stockfish at one of eight strengths and a chosen colour; the game is kept on the device, can be taken back and resumed, and goes to the history when it ends, after the server has checked it.
entities.rationale: Something to play when no friend is around.
acceptanceCriteria: Each strength sets Stockfish's Skill Level and search limit as the README's table gives them.
A finished game is stored only if its moves are legal and it is over or resigned.

origin.description: Gambit's README, written for players and developers.

entities.title: One sign-in for icelander.net
entities.summary: Gambit uses icelander.net's sign-in, with Google or GitHub, like every game on the host.
entities.statement: The game needs a sign-in to icelander.net through its login service; Gambit keeps its own record of each player by address, so a person keeps their games, contacts and history.
entities.rationale: The games are part of icelander.net; and email, name and picture must be known for invitations and contacts.
acceptanceCriteria: Opening the game signed out leads to the host's sign-in and back.
A person known by an older address keeps playing as it.

origin.description: Gambit's README, written for players and developers.
